story_title: A beach town that kept its soul
story: Puerto Vallarta grew up as a fishing village, and the old town has kept its bones: white walls, bougainvillea, steep cobblestone lanes and the crown on top of the church of Our Lady of Guadalupe. The Malecón runs along the water, lined with bronze sculptures, and every evening people lean on the seawall to watch the sun drop into Banderas Bay. Hollywood put the town on the map in the 1960s, and a little of that old glamour never left.

The bay is one of the largest in Mexico, and it shapes everything here. South of town, the coastal road winds past hidden coves and the granite islets of Los Arcos toward Mismaloya. North, the shore curves into Riviera Nayarit: Nuevo Vallarta, Bucerías and finally Punta Mita, where the villas and golf courses sit. Behind it all, the Sierra Madre rises green and close, with jungle restaurants and river pools a short drive up the valleys.
why_title: Why book a private jet to Puerto Vallarta

why.d: At 1 hour 45 minutes from Toluca, Puerto Vallarta works as a Friday departure and a Sunday return, or even a same-day trip for a property viewing or a family event. You set the hours, and domestic flights can be ready about 2 hours after you confirm.

Car seats, strollers, beach bags and surfboards all come along without anyone weighing suitcases at a check-in desk. The kids board without a security line, and everyone lands with energy left for the pool instead of spending it in a terminal.

Many of the villas and resorts sit north of the airport in Riviera Nayarit. Landing at PVR puts you about 15 minutes from Nuevo Vallarta and 45 from Punta Mita, so most of your door-to-door day is the short drive to your villa.

A Learjet 35 for up to 7 passengers starts at $3,000 USD one way, per aircraft, with crew, fuel, catering and permits included. With a full cabin that comes to about $430 per seat. Larger aircraft are quoted in 30 minutes on WhatsApp.

journey_title: Friday afternoon, Mexico City to Banderas Bay

journey.d: Pick the kids up early from school and head west to Toluca on the México-Toluca highway, about an hour by car. Adults only need an official photo ID for this domestic flight, so nobody has to dig out passports.

The car pulls up at the private terminal (FBO) at Toluca International. A quick ID check, your bags go aboard, and you are at the aircraft steps in under 10 minutes from the curb. Snacks and drinks are already on board.

The flight heads west across Michoacán and Jalisco, over volcanic highlands and mountain lakes. Halfway there the ridges start to fall away toward the coast, and the Pacific shows up as a bright line on the horizon.

You land at Puerto Vallarta International after about 1 hour 45 minutes. Jalisco shares Mexico City's time zone, so the clock stays the same. Your car is waiting on the private aviation side of the airport.
Fifteen minutes to the Marina or Nuevo Vallarta, about forty-five to Punta Mita. The kids are in the pool before dark, and you have a margarita in hand when the sun slides into Banderas Bay.

places_title: What to do in Puerto Vallarta after you land

places.name: Zona Romántica
places.d: South of the Río Cuale, the Romantic Zone is the liveliest corner of the old town. Walk out on the Los Muertos Pier at sunset, eat smoked marlin tacos at a street stand, and browse the galleries and cafés along Basilio Badillo. Playa Los Muertos, right below, is the town's favorite beach.

places.name: Islas Marietas
places.d: A protected national park off the northern tip of the bay, about 20 minutes by boat from Punta Mita. Its Hidden Beach sits inside an opening in the rock, reached by swimming through a short tunnel. Access is limited by daily permits, so book a licensed tour early. Blue-footed boobies nest on the cliffs.

places.name: Punta Mita
places.d: The northern tip of Banderas Bay, about 45 minutes from the airport, is a gated peninsula of villas and two Jack Nicklaus golf courses, one with a famous green on a natural island. The surf breaks here are among the best in the region, and the village of El Anclote serves fresh fish on the sand.

places.name: Sayulita
places.d: A barefoot surf town in Riviera Nayarit, about an hour north of the airport. Rent a board for the gentle beach break, wander colorful streets full of boutiques and taquerías, and stay for the sunset. Weekends get busy, so go midweek if your schedule allows.

best_time_title: Best time to fly to Puerto Vallarta
best_time: November through April is the classic season in Puerto Vallarta, with dry, sunny days around 28 degrees Celsius, cool evenings and calm water. From December to March, humpback whales fill Banderas Bay to breed and give birth, and boat tours go out every morning. Christmas, New Year and Semana Santa are the busiest weeks, so confirm your aircraft early for those dates. May is hot and quiet. June through October is the rainy season, with short tropical storms in the afternoon, higher humidity and the jungle at its greenest. The Pacific hurricane season runs from mid-May through November.
airport: Puerto Vallarta International (PVR), officially Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International, is about 900 km from Toluca and sits on the north side of town, between Puerto Vallarta and Nuevo Vallarta. Private aircraft use the general aviation area, away from the commercial terminal, so you walk to your car without crossing the arrivals hall. The Marina is about 5 minutes away, Nuevo Vallarta 15, the Malecón and the Zona Romántica 20 to 25, and Punta Mita about 45 minutes. This is a domestic flight, so there is no customs or immigration.
docs_title: Documents for a private flight to Puerto Vallarta
docs: Your flight to Puerto Vallarta is domestic, so Mexican nationals only need a valid official photo ID, such as an INE card or a passport. Foreign visitors should carry the passport they used to enter Mexico. Send the full name of every passenger on WhatsApp when you confirm, and the aircraft can be ready about 2 hours later. Customs and immigration do not apply on this route.

faq.q: Can I fly to Puerto Vallarta and back the same day?
faq.a: Yes. At 1 hour 45 minutes each way, JETCAB regularly arranges same-day Puerto Vallarta itineraries for property visits, family events and business lunches. You can leave Toluca in the morning, spend the day on the bay and be back home that night.

faq.q: Can you fly a private plane into Mexico?
faq.a: Yes, although foreign aircraft need landing permits and other paperwork. A JETCAB flight from Toluca to Puerto Vallarta is a domestic operation under JETCAB's AFAC operating permit, so there is no international paperwork at all. Each passenger only needs an official photo ID.

faq.q: When is whale season in Puerto Vallarta?
faq.a: Humpback whales arrive in Banderas Bay from about December to March to breed and give birth. Boat tours leave from the Marina and from Punta Mita, and on calm days you can often see whales breaching from the shore. It is also the most popular season to fly in.
